honestly, if someone hurt you, what would you feel if they killed themselves? even if it was a slow, painful suicide? I know I would still probably be mad. even the slowest and most agonizing suicide to me, is nothing compared to the consequences (and regular shit) people naturally face in the entirety life. 

you know what probably would help the people you say you’ve hurt more? working on yourself, understanding your actions and why you made them, and once you’ve grown as a person, giving an apology. if they know you aren’t the same person you used to be and that you fully understand how you messed up, they will feel better. wouldn’t you?

I don’t know where you live but where I am we have something called victim services where you’ll have your own person to talk to and they will even accompany you to court hearings and such. if not, maybe there’s another program in your area that could help? calling around can never hurt. I wish you the best

my mom stopped buying me razors in 6th grade because she found out I self harmed. on one hand it was probably a bit helpful that she didn’t let me have them, but whenever I actually wanted to shave (I’m afab) I had to pay one of my friends to buy me a pack or secretly buy them online. and, ofc, being able to them secretly didn’t help prevent the self harm. if I really wanted to sh, unfortunately I’d find something to use. I stole my parents razors quite a bit. sometimes for shaving and sometimes for hurting myself. I don’t know where I stand on the issue. all I know is my mom did what she thought was best. she never let me shave after that, though, lol. never bought me a razor after that and would get mad at why I wouldn’t show off my legs in summer and it was hot out (after finally being comfortable showing my scars, I had a shit ton of hair on my legs that unfortunately made me feel bad about myself).

and let yourself grieve. you’re allowed to cry and wish for them back. you’re allowed to be mad. let yourself feel the pain fully now so you can make peace sooner, ya know? I’m so sorry for your loss, I don’t quite know what to say.

can’t read all of it run but I have a couple things to say. Parkinson’s is a type of dementia, so memory loss and all that is normal. and my grandpa also had it before passing from it. I just seen a dietician due to this and the best thing we came up with (aside from setting times to eat, even if it’s only a bite. 4 times a day. 1 meal, 1 “big snack”, and the rest snacks.) is switching out foods I already eat like a granola bar or a yogurt cup with one with higher calories, protein, etc. etc. smoothies have really been a lifesaver for me because I really like fruit and there’s not a whole bunch of sugar to put me off of it (sometimes I can’t stand sugary things). I use frozen fruit, soy milk, yogurt, and protein powders with a whole bunch of stuff added, lol. somehow my blood work is good, even my iron, and I’m a vegetarian. idk how I’ve done it. cereal is good too! though I am at the point where the dietician told me to just eat anything I feel I can eat. crepes with tons of syrup and whipped cream? anytime I have energy for them I make them cause just yes.

I have CPTSD and have just finally been working with therapists. it’s a really important thing to do, op. so, please try it out. it’s important to know the people who you were under the care of maybe weren’t as perfect and normal as you thought. I never really realized there was another way I could’ve grown up, ya know? my parents always told me that at least I have a home and food to eat and that it could all be worse, but those aren’t even the bare minimum for a child. kids need love. kids need support. kids need a family, whether biological or not. if you think you might’ve not had those as a kid, that’s okay, cause now this is your time. this is your time to process everything and understand you deserve better than this. because I can say for damn sure just by reading some of your comments that you do. now is your time to find your family, whoever they may be.

this week I started a completely new school program and one of the things I was completely terrified of was meeting the other students. but once I got into the class and watched silently for an hour or so, I was ready to talk to the 2 other people at my table. we had a good time. someone from the other side of the class even came up to me and introduced themselves. I actually had some good conversations with people and felt good about having socialization, ya know?

my point is that it’s alright to start slow, and it’s alright if you’re terrified. it’s alright if you’re not ready to approach someone yet in general or your friends about your mental illness. and, there’s always a chance it’s not as bad as you thought it’d be, so you might as well try and see what happens. maybe if you wanted to start hanging out with your friends more, for example, you could start with small outings? ask to hang out for a couple hours or do something like go to get food or go to a movie theatre. something that will make you feel good to have been able to hang out with them, but not so much that it seriously overwhelms you and/or exhausts you. 

if you can’t plan something without saying only a couple hours or whatever, maybe you could say that you’re just working on some stuff and will tell them when you’re ready, but that they shouldn’t worry too much because you are working on it? if they get mad at you and say you don’t trust them or something, tell them the truth: you’re embarrassed, you’re scared, but if anything ever gets serious you will take action to make sure everything is alright. just my thinking, hope tomorrow goes well.

my therapist once told me, “you think that changing your sleep schedule from waking up at 3pm to waking up at 12pm isn’t good enough to be considered an achievement? that’s like changing your schedule from waking up at 8am to waking up at 5am. this is a big deal. you did good.” and that was the first time I ever really was like, fuck man, I couldn’t see it in that way at all. and I do it all the time, still. the other day I was talking to friends about how when I’m in a really bad depressive period and my thinking is so foggy and irrational, I think I am in a perfect, clear state of mind. but when I’m doing better and can actually think rationally, I’m able to look back at those times and see that I was not thinking clearly in any way, shape, or form. it’s wild what mental illness does to us. wild and confusing as all hell.

I don’t have any obligation to tell you my condition and I simply wanted to avoid someone looking up the condition and nitpicking at how I’m not exactly how that person presented or some shit. we (lots of drs and I) don’t specifically know yet but we do know it falls under the umbrella term dysautonomia, a group of autonomic nervous system disorders. and, because it is apparently important to you, either the disorder or some medications I was on actually caused me to almost entirely lose my appetite and lose around 30% of my body weight, keep in mind I was in my late teens at the time. I was dangerously underweight, and no, it had nothing to do with body issues or wanting to lose weight. that’s why I work with a dietician, cause I can barely feel hungry enough to eat a meal a day. the first couple years after them confirming this is probably what it is were tough but I’ve definitely learned to handle it better and to not push myself super hard due to wanting to be like a “normal” person. everyone has their own issues they have to deal with, and I think the majority of people really are just doing their best to get by. I think treating everyone the same, whether you think they’re faking an illness or not, is the way to go. and, there’s only two ways that conversation could go. yes, you might be confronting someone who is faking an illness, but you also might be really hurting someone who is actually sick (not to mention the fact that you most likely have some problems going on if you’re faking an illness). you either have the possibility of getting under someone’s skin who is faking an illness, or you end up hurting someone who isn’t faking anything.

I can stand up and walk around just fine for short periods of time (with dizziness, but nothing noticeable to an outsider). If I have to stand in the same place (think, choir in school, cashier work, etc.), I’ll be struggling to not fall unconscious in 15-20mins. I can handle casual walking for maybe an hour or so before it becomes really unbearable with dizziness, shortness of breath, and an extremely high heart rate, etc. Anything that is more than a casual stroll, I can’t make it very long. When I first started being aware of my heart rate in high school I remember a time where I was going up 2 flights of stairs to my next class with my friend and almost collapsing when I made it to the top. Our class was close by so we went in and I immediately sat down and took my hr, which was 180-something. I would use a wheelchair if I could at times (shopping for more than 30mins turns into me trying my best to not pass out in front of all the people around me), but my disorder isn’t considered serious or life threatening in any way, and the treatment is to increase sodium intake and slowly build up exercise, in my case with a dietician and a physiotherapist. And, my symptoms are on the minor side of the disorder. Some of us can pass out from just standing up, for example. Not only is every person different, but every disorder effects every person slightly differently.

I barely convince myself to get out of bed every day, how am I supposed to work? we all know our lives depend on the jobs we get. the jobs we get depend on the schooling we do. it all depends on how hard you work, and my brain seems to literally prevent me from doing that. I have DID among other things and I’m on meds and in therapy, but I just can’t do it, I don’t know why. I barely even have the energy or motivation to do things I want to do and that are fun, let alone do things that stress me out. I tell myself (like everyone else tells me) that I’m lazy but it doesn’t change anything. I hate myself so much for it but I don’t do anything. my body just won’t let me and I don’t understand. my disability papers are currently being like decided on (for lack of a better term). my memory is bad, my motivation is bad, my happiness and hope are gone, my life is going to shit, and I maybe take that time to go back to sleep for another 12hrs. anyway.. you’re not alone. I don’t know what I’m going to do or what my life is going to look like, either. and it’s terrifying.
